overview: Sri Kondagattu Anjaneya Swamy Temple is one of the most cherished and spiritually potent Hanuman temples in Telangana. Nestled on a picturesque hillock enveloped by lush forests and flowing streams, close to Kondagattu village in Mallial Mandal, Jagtial district, it is dedicated to Lord Anjaneya (Hanuman). The temple is renowned as a divine-healing shrine providing relief from Shani Dosha, fear, mental stress, legal issues, and negative planetary influences. For generations, devotees from Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Karnataka have flocked here in search of strength, courage, and divine protection.
summary: Sri Kondagattu Anjaneya Swamy Temple is a historic Hanuman temple in Muthyampet village, Mallial Mandal, Jagtial District, Telangana. Per local tradition it is associated with the Treta Yuga (Lord Hanuman pausing here while carrying the Sanjeevani mountain), while the present shrine is said to have been founded ~300 years ago by a cowherd guided by a vision of Hanuman and later renovated ~160 years ago by Krishna Rao Deshmukh. The complex features two large Anjaneya idols and shrines to Venkateswara, Lakshmi, Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and Shiva. It is famed for Shani Dosha relief, a believed 40-day puja for childless couples, and Hanuman Jayanti, which draws an estimated 4 lakh devotees annually.

history.content: Per local folklore, the temple's history stretches back to the Treta Yuga. Lord Hanuman is believed to have paused at this hill to recharge his strength while transporting the Sanjeevani mountain to save Lakshmana during the Ramayana battle; a fragment of the mountain is said to have become the present-day Kondagattu hill. The surrounding forest offered a bounty of medicinal herbs, and later sages sensed the divine presence and installed the idol here.

sthala_puranam: The name 'Kondagattu' is derived from the Telugu words 'Konda' (hill) and 'Gattu' (embankment or edge), capturing the temple's hilltop location. Per local tradition, while carrying the Sanjeevani mountain to revive Lakshmana, Lord Hanuman passed over the Mutyampeta region and a fragment of the mountain became the present-day Kondagattu hill, where he paused to rest. The lush forest around offered medicinal herbs, and sages later installed the idol here. Per Telangana360, about 300 years ago a cowherd named Singam Sanjeevudu, after losing one of his buffalos, came to this hillock searching for it and slept here. Lord Anjaneya came into his dream and told him the whereabouts of his buffalo. As he woke up and looked around the hillock, he found an illuminating idol of Anjaneya, and he then built a small temple for the lord at the current location.
religious_significance: Kondagattu is one of the most frequented Hanuman temples in South India and a prominent Hanuman pilgrimage centre in Telangana. It represents a unique blend of folk faith and Ramayana reverence, with community worship that brings together people of all castes. It is especially famed for the Shani Dosha Parihara Pooja and Vahana Pooja.
spiritual_significance: Lord Anjaneya is revered here as a divine healer addressing both physical and mental health issues. Devotees believe worship here provides relief from Shani Dosha, eases mental stress and depression, resolves legal and financial difficulties, dispels fear and negative energies, and (via a 40-day puja) can bless childless couples with a child.

architecture: The temple's architecture is beautifully simple yet radiates deep spiritual energy. Inside, Lord Anjaneya is depicted in a standing posture exuding strength and grace. The temple is embraced by natural rock formations, and the complex features two large Anjaneya idols with separate shrines to Lord Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, Lord Shiva, Venkateswara and Lakshmi. A pradakshina path winds around the hill for circumambulation, and the surrounding lush forest creates a serene atmosphere ideal for meditation and devotion. The Temple is decorated with sculptures of Gods and Goddesses on its facades and walls. Stairs have been provided to help visitors go up to view the statue from close quarters.

accommodation.availability: A limited number of rooms and dormitory-style accommodations are available for devotees. Basic amenities such as mats, bedding and sanitary facilities are provided; devotees should bring personal essentials. Per Tripadvisor Aditya G review, the Haritha Hotel (Telangana Tourism) is 200 m away and is well-maintained; another hotel 'Shreyans' is also nearby. Private lodges in Karimnagar or Jagtial are also options.
accommodation.booking_process: No online advance booking is available. Devotees must check in and register for a room at the temple's accommodation counter on arrival. For hotels, book via standard hotel booking platforms or the Haritha Hotel booking.
accommodation.first_come_basis: Rooms are assigned on a first-come, first-served basis, especially on Saturdays, Sundays and festival days.
accommodation.price_range: Temple-managed rooms are budget-friendly, typically ₹150–₹500 per night (price confirmed at the counter). Private lodges in Karimnagar or Jagtial generally range from ~₹800 to ₹2,000+ per night. Haritha Hotel (Telangana Tourism) is the recommended option.

best_time_to_visit: Saturdays and Tuesdays see significantly higher pilgrim footfall, with Saturdays drawing the largest crowds and considered most auspicious. October to March offers pleasant weather; avoid sweltering summer afternoons. Hanuman Jayanti is the most significant occasion but extremely crowded (estimated 4 lakh devotees).

introduction.en: Sri Kondagattu Anjaneya Swamy Temple is one of the most cherished and spiritually potent Hanuman temples in Telangana. Set on a forested hillock in Mallial Mandal of Jagtial district, it is dedicated to Lord Anjaneya and is revered as a divine-healing shrine for relief from Shani Dosha, fear, mental stress, and legal troubles. Devotees from across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka flock here for strength, courage and divine protection.

history.en: Per local folklore the site dates to the Treta Yuga: Lord Hanuman is believed to have paused here while carrying the Sanjeevani mountain to revive Lakshmana, and a fragment of that mountain became the Kondagattu hill. Per Telangana360, about 300 years ago a cowherd named Singam Sanjeevudu, after losing his buffalo, was guided by a vision of Hanuman and built a small temple here. The present structure was renovated ~160 years ago by Krishna Rao Deshmukh. Hanuman Jayanti here draws an estimated four lakh devotees annually.

travel_guide.en: Kondagattu is about 178-210 kilometres from Hyderabad on the Karimnagar-Jagtial highway, with regular TSRTC buses; it is roughly 35-39 kilometres from Karimnagar and 14-20 kilometres from Jagtial. The nearest railway stations are Jagtial and Karimnagar, and the nearest airport is Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (~248 km). The temple is open from about 4:00 AM to 8:30 PM (or 6:00 AM-1:00 PM + 4:00 PM-8:00 PM, varies by source), with extended hours on Saturdays and festival days. October to March is the best season to visit. Stay at Haritha Hotel (200 m away) for a well-maintained experience.

faq.question: Where can I find Kondagattu Anjaneya Swamy Temple?
faq.answer: Kondagattu Anjaneya Swamy Temple is in Kondagattu village, within the Mallial Mandal of Jagtial district, Telangana, roughly 35-39 km from Karimnagar.

faq.question: Who is the deity worshipped at Kondagattu Temple?
faq.answer: The temple is dedicated to Lord Anjaneya (Hanuman), revered here as a mighty healer and protector.

faq.question: What makes Kondagattu Temple spiritually significant?
faq.answer: It is well-known for providing relief from Shani Dosha, mental stress, fear, legal troubles and health issues. Devotees believe Lord Hanuman serves as a divine healer here. A 40-day puja is believed to bless childless couples with a child.

faq.question: What are the visiting hours for Kondagattu Temple?
faq.answer: Typically, the temple welcomes visitors from 6:00 AM to 1:00 PM and again from 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (Tue/Sat/Sun: 6 AM-4:30 PM and 6-8 PM; rest of days: 6 AM-1:30 PM, 3 PM-4:30 PM, 6 PM-8 PM per Tripadvisor review). Daily Abhishekam at 9:00 AM. Hours may be extended on Sundays, Saturdays and festival days.

faq.question: Is there an entry fee for darshan?
faq.answer: No, general darshan is free for all devotees. There are nominal charges for special sevas.

faq.question: What are the key sevas performed at the temple?
faq.answer: The main sevas include Abhishekam (daily 9 AM), Vada Mala, Tailabhishekam, Archana, Sahasranama Pooja, and Shani Dosha Parihara Pooja (particularly on Saturdays).

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Kondagattu Temple?
faq.answer: Saturdays, Sundays and Hanuman Jayanti are considered especially auspicious, with Saturdays drawing the largest crowds. October to March is the best season weather-wise.

faq.question: Is there accommodation available near the temple?
faq.answer: Yes, there are limited temple rooms and dormitories available on a first-come, first-served basis. The Haritha Hotel (Telangana Tourism) is 200 m away and well-maintained. Many devotees opt to stay in Karimnagar or Jagtial for more comfortable facilities.

faq.question: How much does it cost to book a room at Kondagattu Temple?
faq.answer: Temple room charges are quite reasonable, typically ranging from ₹150 to ₹500 per night, depending on availability and the season.
